title: Current growth in an RL circuit
caption: With L = 0.5 H, R = 10 Ω and ε = 12 V, the time constant is τ = L/R = 0.05 s and the final current ε/R = 1.2 A. The current rises as I = I_max(1 − e^{−t/τ}): after one τ (0.05 s) it is 1.2 × (1 − e⁻¹) = 0.76 A, 63% of the way. The inductor opposes the change, so the current cannot jump.
alt: Graph of current against time: a rise from 0 towards 1.2 A, reaching 0.76 A at 0.05 s.
description: The horizontal axis is time in seconds; the vertical axis is the current in amperes.
The current starts at 0 (the inductor opposes sudden change) and approaches ε/R = 1.2 A.

checks.name: initial rate of rise = ε/L = 24 A/s
